concepts.title: Farm and Non-Farm Occupations in Rural Areas

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Farm and Non-Farm Occupations in Rural Areas' refers to.
questions.a: Rural economies comprise agricultural work such as crop cultivation alongside diverse non-farm trades including craft-making, retail shops, repair services, and transportation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Farm and Non-Farm Occupations in Rural Areas'.
questions.a: Rural livelihoods extend beyond crop cultivation to incorporate local service industries and craft production.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Farm and Non-Farm Occupations in Rural Areas' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Kalpattu village (source: fess308.txt lines 30-65)

concepts.title: Wage Earners and Agricultural Labour Income

questions.q: Calculate total income earned by an agricultural labourer over a given number of days. Use the method 'Wage Earners and Agricultural Labour Income'. Work with: daily_wage = 50, days_worked = 240. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_income.
questions.a: 12000 units

questions.q: Find the seasonal earnings of a landless farm worker. Use the method 'Wage Earners and Agricultural Labour Income'. Work with: daily_wage = 50, days_worked = 300. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_income.
questions.a: 15000 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Wage Earners and Agricultural Labour Income' refers to.
questions.a: Landless agricultural workers sell their manual labor during farming seasons for daily wages, facing low pay and lack of year-round employment.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Wage Earners and Agricultural Labour Income'.
questions.a: Agricultural labourers experience seasonal employment gaps and low wage rates due to landlessness.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Wage Earners and Agricultural Labour Income', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: total_income = daily_wage * days_worked

concepts.title: Small Farmers and Crop Loan Obligations

questions.q: Find the remaining paddy bags available for household consumption after repaying a crop loan. Use the method 'Small Farmers and Crop Loan Obligations'. Work with: loan_repayment_bags = 400, total_paddy_bags = 24. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_paddy_retained.
questions.a: -376 units

questions.q: Calculate paddy retained by a small farmer after settling input debts. Use the method 'Small Farmers and Crop Loan Obligations'. Work with: loan_repayment_bags = 300, total_paddy_bags = 24. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_paddy_retained.
questions.a: -276 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Small Farmers and Crop Loan Obligations' refers to.
questions.a: Smallholders cultivate limited acreage primarily using family labour and often depend on trade loans for inputs, obligating them to sell produce below market prices.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Small Farmers and Crop Loan Obligations'.
questions.a: Small-scale agriculturalists face income shortfalls and trader loan commitments that reduce marketable surplus.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Small Farmers and Crop Loan Obligations', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: net_paddy_retained = total_paddy_bags - loan_repayment_bags

concepts.title: Causes and Dynamics of Rural Debt Trap

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Causes and Dynamics of Rural Debt Trap' refers to.
questions.a: A cycle of compounding debt occurs when crop failure or health emergencies force farmers to borrow repeatedly, exceeding their capacity to repay.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Causes and Dynamics of Rural Debt Trap'.
questions.a: High interest rates, bad seeds, monsoon failure, and distress borrowing lead to persistent rural indebtedness.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Causes and Dynamics of Rural Debt Trap' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: On being in Debt (source: fess308.txt lines 185-210)

concepts.title: Large Farmers and Diversified Rural Enterprises

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Large Farmers and Diversified Rural Enterprises' refers to.
questions.a: Wealthy agrarian landowners operate large acreage, employ hired labor, and expand capital into processing mills, trade, and financial lending.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Large Farmers and Diversified Rural Enterprises'.
questions.a: Large farmers generate substantial surpluses enabling investment in off-farm commercial ventures.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Large Farmers and Diversified Rural Enterprises' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Ramalingam and Karuthamma (source: fess308.txt lines 215-235)

concepts.title: Categorization and Proportions of Indian Farmers

questions.q: Calculate the number of small farmers in a region given the total farmer population. Use the method 'Categorization and Proportions of Indian Farmers'. Work with: total_farmers = 240. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of small_farmer_count.
questions.a: 192 units

questions.q: Find the count of small landholders using the national eighty percent proportion. Use the method 'Categorization and Proportions of Indian Farmers'. Work with: total_farmers = 40. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of small_farmer_count.
questions.a: 32 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Categorization and Proportions of Indian Farmers' refers to.
questions.a: Indian agriculture is dominated by smallholders (80%) and landless laborers (40% of rural families), while large landholders comprise only 20% of farmers.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Categorization and Proportions of Indian Farmers'.
questions.a: Most cultivators in India operate marginal plots insufficient for full year-round subsistence.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Categorization and Proportions of Indian Farmers', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: small_farmer_count = total_farmers * 80 / 100

concepts.title: Terrace Farming and Community Labour in Hilly Regions

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Terrace Farming and Community Labour in Hilly Regions' refers to.
questions.a: Slope cultivation technique where hillside land is carved into stepped flat terraces with raised borders to retain water for paddy growth.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Terrace Farming and Community Labour in Hilly Regions'.
questions.a: Terrace carving enables hillside irrigation and rice cultivation through collective group labor.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Terrace Farming and Community Labour in Hilly Regions' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Terrace Farming in Nagaland (source: fess308.txt lines 270-300)

concepts.title: Forest Gathering and Supplementary Rural Livelihoods

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Forest Gathering and Supplementary Rural Livelihoods' refers to.
questions.a: Non-wood forest produce collection, livestock rearing, and dairy cooperative sales provide essential supplementary earnings for rural households.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Forest Gathering and Supplementary Rural Livelihoods'.
questions.a: Rural families rely on natural resource gathering and animal husbandry to supplement seasonal farming income.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Forest Gathering and Supplementary Rural Livelihoods' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Terrace Farming in Nagaland (source: fess308.txt lines 305-325)

concepts.title: Coastal Fishing Economy and Revenue Share Calculation

questions.q: Calculate individual share value from total fish auction revenue divided into equal parts. Use the method 'Coastal Fishing Economy and Revenue Share Calculation'. Work with: total_auction_revenue = 50000, total_shares = 75. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of share_amount.

Find the per-share payout from daily catch earnings. Use the method 'Coastal Fishing Economy and Revenue Share Calculation'. Work with: total_auction_revenue = 80000, total_shares = 40. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of share_amount.
questions.a: 2000 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Coastal Fishing Economy and Revenue Share Calculation' refers to.
questions.a: Maritime fishing livelihoods depend on equipment investment and daily auctioning of catch, where revenues are divided into designated functional shares.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Coastal Fishing Economy and Revenue Share Calculation'.
questions.a: Fish catch proceeds are distributed among crew members and equipment owners, with seasonal fishing bans requiring lean-period loans.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Coastal Fishing Economy and Revenue Share Calculation', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: share_amount = total_auction_revenue / total_shares
